# `silk/text/byte_search`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Fast searches over byte slices: the first or last position of a byte, the first of two or
three bytes, the number of times a byte occurs, and the first position of a byte sequence.

## When to use
Use these functions instead of a byte-by-byte loop when scanning text or binary data, for
example to find the end of a line, a delimiter or a header name.

## Details
On CPUs with 128-bit vectors (x86-64, AArch64, and wasm32 with `simd128`), each function
compares sixteen bytes at a time with `silk.simd.u8x16` and finishes the last bytes one by
one. Elsewhere it is a plain loop. The results are the same everywhere; only the speed
differs. [`findSlice`](#findSlice) filters candidates by the first and last byte of the needle, then
compares the whole needle at each candidate.

## Examples
### Split off the first line
```silk
import silk.text.byte_search
import silk.core.option { Option }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let text = b"GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: example.com\r\n"
  let end = match byte_search.findSlice(text, b"\r\n") {
    Option<usize>.Some { value } => value
    Option<usize>.None => { return 1 }
  }
  if end != 14 || byte_search.count(text, 10) != 2 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `byte_search` with `import silk.text.byte_search as byte_search`.

## `find`

```silk
pub fn find(haystack: &[u8], wanted: u8) -> Option<usize>
```

Returns the index of the first byte of `haystack` equal to `wanted`, or none.

<a id="findSlice"></a>

## `findSlice`

```silk
pub fn findSlice(haystack: &[u8], needle: &[u8]) -> Option<usize>
```

Returns the index where `needle` first occurs in `haystack`, or none. An empty `needle`
occurs at `0`.
